finding.summary: A condition-blind outcome observer is necessary but not sufficient for semantic-content causality. G9 can still appear to show A-vs-B semantic influence if payload_ref, candidate identity, arm identity, expected-result metadata, or other treatment-correlated identifiers reach the recipient/executor/task context through a path other than the validated broadcast payload itself.
finding.why_distinct_from_existing_sham_fence: The existing sham-control fence correctly requires matched mechanism and a treatment-blind evaluator. This additional fence targets leakage upstream of the evaluator: recipient/executor behavior can be conditioned on an opaque payload or arm identity and then produce a clean-looking downstream semantic difference even though the semantic bytes were not the causal variable.
finding.risk: Without an identifier-independence test, a four-trial counterbalanced crossover can establish correlation with treatment assignment while still failing to isolate semantic content as the operative cause.

counterexample.setup: Both arms use the same delivery/uptake/reentry machinery and the outcome scorer receives no treatment label. The executor nevertheless receives payload_ref=A or payload_ref=B through task configuration, process arguments, environment, workspace key, filename, plan metadata, recipient routing metadata, or another side channel.
counterexample.bad_behavior: The executor maps opaque identifier A to semantic outcome X and opaque identifier B to semantic outcome Y without consulting the delivered semantic payload bytes.
counterexample.false_positive: All visible G9 crossover checks may look satisfied: matched mechanism, successful reentry, stable same-arm repeats, different A/B outcomes, and a condition-blind scorer. Yet the causal variable is the leaked identifier, not GWT semantic content.

required_fences: Recipient/executor/task-context inputs must be treatment-invariant except for the validated broadcast semantic payload itself and unavoidable causal transport state required to deliver that payload.

Do not expose treatment arm, expected result, payload_ref, candidate_id, payload label, semantic digest, or equivalent treatment-correlated identity to behavioral computation through process arguments, environment, filenames, workspace keys, plan metadata, routing metadata, task input, pre-state, or recipient configuration.

Exact payload lineage may be recorded for evidence, but identity joining should occur post hoc in the evidence binder after the downstream behavior is observed rather than being supplied as a behavioral feature.
The outcome observer/scorer must remain blind to treatment/mechanism labels as already required by the sham-control fence.

Counterbalancing must preserve task input, pre-state, source, boot/context identity, executor plan, recipient mechanics, timing budget, and scoring path across arms so only semantic payload content is intentionally varied.

hard_negatives.test: Deliver identical semantic payload bytes twice while changing only opaque payload_ref/candidate labels in the evidence layer.
hard_negatives.required_result: Downstream semantic behavior must remain invariant. Any behavioral difference indicates identifier leakage or an unmodelled confound and blocks semantic-content causal admission.

hard_negatives.test: Swap A/B opaque identifiers while keeping the actually delivered semantic bytes fixed and keeping recipient/executor inputs otherwise identical.
hard_negatives.required_result: Outcome must follow delivered semantic content, not the swapped identifier.

hard_negatives.test: Hold all non-content recipient/executor/task inputs fixed while swapping only the validated semantic payload content across counterbalanced positions.
hard_negatives.required_result: A candidate content-causal effect requires the downstream semantic outcome to track the delivered content across the swap while same-content repeats remain stable.

hard_negatives.test: Materialize or hash the recipient/executor behavioral input surface for every arm and compare it field-by-field before outcome generation.
hard_negatives.required_result: No treatment-correlated field may differ except the admitted semantic content channel and transport fields proven necessary for that delivery.

hard_negatives.test: Run behavioral computation without payload_ref/arm identity available, then join the exact payload lineage only after the outcome has been produced.
hard_negatives.required_result: The discriminator must remain evaluable and preserve the same content-following result. If identity is required before behavior, semantic-content causality remains unisolated.

promotion_rule: A downstream difference correlated with payload_ref, arm identity, candidate identity, expected-result metadata, or another treatment side channel is not evidence of semantic GWT content causality. Semantic-content candidate credit must remain zero unless behavior follows the actually delivered semantic content under matched mechanism/context and treatment identity is unavailable to behavioral computation except through that validated content path.
next_exact_action: The active G9 owner should absorb this packet as hard-negative regression guidance without creating a competing generation: make treatment-correlated identifiers unavailable to recipient/executor/task behavioral computation, add identifier relabelling/ref-swap/content-swap negatives, keep lineage joining post hoc, then run the existing G9 repository discriminator. Only after exact repository CI is green should one exact source be frozen for owner-VPS target execution.
